The gate starts at 0.05 and remains below 0.1; the first valid state is unchanged. Training readouts remain causal. The generated predictor imports this same model class and restores its gate through the existing state_dict loader, so no predictor-writer change is necessary.

def aggregate_states(self, out: torch.Tensor, seq: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Prefix normalization yields weight 2**(-age/5) at every valid step.
        positions = torch.arange(seq.size(1), device=out.device, dtype=torch.float32)
        weights = torch.exp2((positions - (seq.size(1) - 1)) / 5.0)
        weights = weights.unsqueeze(0) * seq.ne(0).float()
        numerator = torch.cumsum(out.float() * weights.unsqueeze(-1), dim=1)
        denominator = torch.cumsum(weights, dim=1).unsqueeze(-1)
        pooled = numerator / denominator.clamp_min(torch.finfo(torch.float32).tiny)

edits.replace:
def aggregate_states(self, out: torch.Tensor, seq: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        valid = seq.ne(0)
        positions = torch.arange(seq.size(1), device=seq.device).expand_as(seq)
        latest = positions.masked_fill(~valid, -1).cummax(dim=1).values
        previous_positions = torch.cat(
            (torch.full_like(latest[:, :1], -1), latest[:, :-1]), dim=1
        )
        previous = out.gather(
            1,
            previous_positions.clamp_min(0).unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(out),
        )
        has_previous = valid & previous_positions.ge(0)
        gate = (0.1 * torch.sigmoid(self.readout_logit)).to(out.dtype)
        gate = gate * has_previous.unsqueeze(-1).to(out.dtype)
        return (1.0 - gate) * out + gate * previous
